B. Vitamin B1 — 2. Bleeding
C. Vitamin K — 3. Night blindness
D. Iodine — 4. Goitre
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, B1 beri-beri, K bleeding and iodine goitre.

s: Deficiency of which vitamin causes pernicious anaemia?
x: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia; B1 causes beri-beri, B3 pellagra and C scurvy.

s: Rickets is caused by the deficiency of which vitamin?
x: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets; vitamin C causes scurvy, A night blindness and K bleeding.

s: Which measure is low in children suffering from wasting?
x: Wasting is low weight-for-height; stunting is low height-for-age and underweight low weight-for-age.

s: Which of the following correctly presents the NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 figures for underweight children?
x: Underweight declined from 32.1% in NFHS-5 to 31.8% in NFHS-6. The 35.8% figure belongs to NFHS-4.

s: According to NFHS-5, anaemia affected approximately what proportions of children aged 6–59 months and women aged 15–49 years respectively?
x: NFHS-5 reported anaemia among 67.1% of children aged 6–59 months and 57.0% of women aged 15–49 years.

s: Underweight prevalence was highest among which of the following social groups according to NFHS-5?
o: Other Backward Classes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Scheduled Tribes, followed by Scheduled Castes
Scheduled Castes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Urban households, followed by rural households
x: Underweight was highest among Scheduled Tribes at 44.1%, followed by Scheduled Castes at 39.1%. It was also higher in rural areas.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 findings for children under five years?
x: Stunting fell from 35.5% in NFHS-5 to 29.3% in NFHS-6. Options A and D reverse the order of the underweight (32.1% → 31.8%) and severe-wasting (7.7% → 5.2%) figures, and the breastfeeding figures in C are not among the stated NFHS findings.

s: Which measure is low in stunted children?
x: Stunting is low height-for-age; wasting is low weight-for-height and underweight is low weight-for-age.

s: According to NFHS-5, what was the stunting rate among children in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's stunting was 31.2% in NFHS-5 (25% in NFHS-6); 35.5% is the national figure.

s: Which measure is low in an underweight child?
x: Underweight means low weight-for-age; stunting is low height-for-age and wasting is low weight-for-height.

s: According to NFHS-6, what was the stunting rate among children in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's stunting fell from 31.2% (NFHS-5) to 25% (NFHS-6); 29.3% is the all-India NFHS-6 figure.

s: According to NFHS-6, which State recorded high child wasting and underweight?
x: Madhya Pradesh showed high child wasting and underweight; Meghalaya showed a decline in stunting.

s: Under WHO's classification, overweight, obesity and diet-related NCDs are counted as forms of:
x: WHO's malnutrition in all its forms covers undernutrition, inadequate vitamins and minerals, and overweight, obesity and diet-related NCDs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about malnutrition burdens?
o: SOFI 2025's 'triple burden' is wasting, stunting and underweight
Wasting, stunting and underweight are all forms of undernutrition
The 'double burden' is undernutrition and overnutrition occurring together
A Vellore cohort study found thinness and overweight rising sharply between ages 7 and 9
x: SOFI 2025's triple burden is undernutrition, micronutrient deficiency/anaemia and overweight.

s: The 'triple burden' of malnutrition (SOFI 2025) adds which of the following to undernutrition and overweight?
x: The triple burden is undernutrition plus micronutrient deficiency/anaemia plus overweight.

s: According to SOFI 2025, what is India's child wasting rate, the world's highest?
x: SOFI 2025 puts India's wasting at 18.7% (21 million), the world's highest.

s: Which State was noted in NFHS-6 for a decline in child stunting?
x: NFHS-6 noted a decline in stunting in Meghalaya, while Madhya Pradesh had high wasting and underweight.

s: Food insecurity and poverty may lead to both undernutrition and overnutrition through the consumption of which kind of food?
o: Only locally produced fruits and vegetables
x: Food insecurity and poverty can produce undernutrition while also encouraging consumption of inexpensive energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods that contribute to overnutrition.

s: Which one of the following is regarded as the main driver of malnutrition in India?
o: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
x: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity are the main driver of malnutrition (APPSC 2025 key). Fortified rice is a remedy, not a cause; women's schooling improves child nutrition; overuse of supplements is not cited as a driver.

s: According to NFHS-5, what share of women had 10 or more years of schooling?
x: NFHS-5 found 41% of women had 10+ years of schooling, a driver of child nutrition.

s: With which programme is the 6x6x6 strategy associated?
o: Rice fortification under the Public Distribution System
x: Anemia Mukt Bharat uses a 6x6x6 strategy consisting of six interventions, six target groups and six institutional mechanisms.

s: With which nutrients is the rice supplied through the PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN fortified?
o: Calcium, vitamin C and vitamin D
Iron, folic acid and vitamin B12
Iodine, zinc and vitamin A only
x: The specified fortified rice contains iron, folic acid and vitamin B12 and is supplied through the PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh scheme provides a nutritious meal along with iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis?
x: Anna Amrutha Hastam provides a nutritious meal and iron-folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis.

s: YSR Sampoorna Poshana Plus covers pregnant women, lactating mothers and children in how many tribal mandals?
x: YSR Sampoorna Poshana Plus (Sep 2020) covers the same groups in 77 tribal mandals.

s: Who is the main target group of Anna Amrutha Hastam in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Anna Amrutha Hastam gives pregnant and lactating women a nutritious meal and iron-folic acid tablets through Anganwadis.

s: In which year were YSR Sampoorna Poshana and YSR Sampoorna Poshana Plus launched in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Both schemes were launched in September 2020; the Plus version covers 77 tribal mandals.

s: The Under-Five Mortality Rate (U5MR) is expressed per how many live births?
x: U5MR, like IMR, uses a base of 1,000 live births; only the MMR uses 1,00,000.

s: According to SRS 2023, what was India's IMR?
x: The IMR was 25 according to SRS 2023, as cited in the Economic Survey 2025-26. The figures 28 and 35.2 refer to older or different sources.

s: As per SRS 2018-20, what was India's Maternal Mortality Ratio (maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births)?
x: India's MMR was 97 per 1,00,000 live births in SRS 2018-20. 25 is India's IMR (SRS 2023), which is per 1,000 live births; 45 is Andhra Pradesh's MMR; 130 is not the SRS 2018-20 figure.

s: What was India's Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in 2016?
According to SRS 2020-22, what was India's Maternal Mortality Ratio?
x: MMR fell from 97 (2018-20) to 93 (2019-21) and 88 (SRS 2020-22); 45 is AP's MMR.

s: The Neonatal Mortality Rate counts the deaths of infants within what period after birth?
x: NMR counts deaths in the first 28 days per 1,000 live births.

s: The Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is expressed per how many live births?
x: MMR counts maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births, while IMR and U5MR use 1,000 live births.

s: What was India's Infant Mortality Rate in 2013?
x: India's IMR was 40 in 2013, 39 in 2014, 37 in 2015 and 34 in 2016.

s: According to NFHS-5, what was India's infant mortality rate?
x: NFHS-5 survey values were IMR 35.2 and U5MR 41.9; 25 is the SRS 2023 figure.

s: Which State is credited with having the lowest IMR owing to adequate basic health and education facilities?
x: Kerala has the lowest IMR, attributed to adequate basic health and education facilities.

s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Andhra Pradesh health indicators is correctly matched?
x: Andhra Pradesh has an MMR of 45 and an IMR of 24, both better than the corresponding national averages.

s: As per SRS 2020, what was Andhra Pradesh's Infant Mortality Rate?
x: AP's IMR was 24 against India's 28 (SRS 2020); 35 was AP's NFHS-4 value.

s: What was Telangana's Infant Mortality Rate as reported in 2026?
x: Telangana reported IMR 18, MMR 43 and TFR 1.5 (2026); AP's IMR is 24 and India's 25.

s: As per SRS 2020, what was the crude birth rate of Andhra Pradesh?
x: SRS 2020 gives AP a crude birth rate of 15.7 against India's 19.5; 6.3 is AP's crude death rate.

s: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with which institution serving as the nodal agency?
o: Indian Council of Medical Research, Hyderabad
International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
x: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai, is the nodal agency.

s: According to NFHS-5, which statement regarding sex ratio is correct?
o: The overall sex ratio was 1020; the rural ratio was 1,037 and the urban ratio was 985.
The overall sex ratio was 920, with the rural ratio lower than the urban ratio.
The overall sex ratio was 985; the rural ratio was 1,020 and the urban ratio was 1,037.
The overall sex ratio was 1,037, while both rural and urban ratios were below 1,000.
x: NFHS-5 reported an overall sex ratio of 1020, with 1,037 in rural areas and 985 in urban areas. The figure 920 refers to the child sex ratio mentioned separately.

s: How does the National Family Health Survey report child malnutrition?
o: As one single overall malnutrition percentage
As wasting alone, excluding stunting and underweight
As stunting, wasting and underweight separately
x: NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight as separate indicators and gives no single overall malnutrition percentage.

s: In which year was NFHS-2 conducted?
x: NFHS-1 was in 1992-93, NFHS-2 in 1998-99, NFHS-3 in 2005-06 and NFHS-4 in 2015-16.

s: Which of the following was NOT included in NFHS-5?
x: NFHS-5 included pre-school education, menstrual hygiene and NCD screening, but not the HIV test.

s: In which year was NFHS-6 conducted?
x: NFHS-6 was conducted in 2023-24 and its results came in 2026; NFHS-5 was 2019-21.

s: What was the child sex ratio according to NFHS-5?
x: NFHS-5 gave a child sex ratio of 920 (Census 2011: 918); 1020 is the overall sex ratio.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct according to the SRS abridged life tables for 2016–20?
o: Andhra Pradesh's male life expectancy was 69.1 years
India's male life expectancy was 68.6 years
India's female life expectancy was 71.4 years
Andhra Pradesh's female life expectancy was lower than India's
x: AP's female life expectancy was 72.2 years, higher than India's 71.4 years.

s: What was the approximate life expectancy in India at the time of Independence?
x: Life expectancy at Independence was approximately 32 years.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, what was India's life expectancy in 2023?
x: Life expectancy rose from 49.7 years (1973) to 70.3 years (2023); 68.3 is the older SRS 2011-15 figure and 72.2 is AP's female figure.

s: As per SRS abridged life tables 2016-20, what was the female life expectancy in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's female life expectancy was 72.2 years, higher than India's 71.4; 69.1 is AP's male figure.

s: What is the replacement level of Total Fertility Rate?
x: Replacement-level TFR is 2.1.

s: According to NFHS-5, India's Total Fertility Rate fell from 2.2 to what level?
x: NFHS-5 shows India's TFR at 2.0, below the replacement level of 2.1.

s: Which State had the highest Total Fertility Rate in NFHS-5?
x: Bihar had the highest TFR (3.0), followed by Meghalaya (2.9) and Uttar Pradesh (2.4).

s:
Consider the following statements about Total Fertility Rate:
1. Andhra Pradesh's TFR is 1.5.
2. Five States were still above the replacement level in NFHS-5.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP's TFR is 1.5, and five States (Bihar, Meghalaya, UP, Jharkhand, Manipur) were above 2.1 in NFHS-5.

s: What does the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) measure?
o: The average number of children a woman would bear in her reproductive years
The number of births per 1,000 population in a year
The number of women per 1,000 men
The number of infant deaths per 1,000 live births
x: TFR is the average number of children a woman would bear during her reproductive years; 2.1 is the replacement level.

s: Which of the following States had a Total Fertility Rate above the replacement level in NFHS-5?
x: Five States were above 2.1 in NFHS-5: Bihar, Meghalaya, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Manipur; AP and Telangana are at 1.5.

s: Which of the following States was NOT above the replacement-level TFR in NFHS-5?
x: Andhra Pradesh's TFR is 1.5, well below 2.1; Bihar (3.0), UP (2.4) and Jharkhand (2.3) were above it.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six services provided through Anganwadi Services?
x: The six services include supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, nutrition and health education, immunisation, health check-up and referral services. Old-age pension distribution is not one of them.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about POSHAN Abhiyaan?
o: It works through convergence of ICDS, NHM and Swachh Bharat
It aims to reduce stunting, wasting, anaemia and low birth weight
It is under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018) is under the Ministry of Women and Child Development, not the Health Ministry.

s: Anganwadi Services under ICDS cover children of which age group, besides pregnant and lactating women?
x: Anganwadi Services cover children from six months to six years, and pregnant and lactating women.

s: PM POSHAN, launched in 2021, was renamed from which scheme?
x: PM POSHAN (2021) replaced the Mid-Day Meal scheme and covers Classes I–VIII plus Bal Vatika.

s: Which students are covered by PM POSHAN in government and aided schools?
o: Classes I to VIII, plus Bal Vatika
x: PM POSHAN, renamed from Mid-Day Meal in 2021, covers Classes I-VIII and pre-primary Bal Vatika.
